title: SaGE: Evaluating Moral Consistency in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: The paper assesses moral consistency by generating paraphrased versions of moral questions (using the Moral Consistency Corpus derived from MIC) and measuring the entropy of the semantic graph (SaGE) constructed from the model's answers and generated 'Rules of Thumb' (RoTs) to determine if the model maintains consistent moral judgments across semantically equivalent scenarios.

The paper utilizes the TruthfulQA dataset, which is designed to measure whether models mimic human falsehoods and cognitive biases, to evaluate the relationship between the model's task accuracy (truthfulness) and its semantic consistency (SaGE scores) across paraphrased inputs.
